What Is the Weather Like in Manali in June?

June is one of the most popular months to visit Manali, and the weather can genuinely surprise you. Days are pleasant and mild — typically 15°C to 25°C — but evenings drop sharply to 8°C or below. Mountain winds add to the chill factor. Rain is possible as pre-monsoon conditions begin.

The key principle for dressing in Manali in June: layering. You need to be able to add and remove layers as conditions change throughout the day.

Outfit 1 — Sightseeing (Hadimba Temple, Mall Road, Solang Valley)

The base: A well-fitted cotton or merino t-shirt. Avoid thick winter tees — you'll be walking and the daytime sun can be warm.

The middle layer: A light full-sleeve shirt or a thin sweatshirt. This is what you'll wear when the breeze picks up.

The outer layer: A packable windbreaker or a light fleece jacket. Essential for Rohtang, Solang and any higher-altitude spot.

Bottoms: Comfortable jeans or trekking trousers. Avoid shorts — they offer no protection from mountain winds and most temples require covered knees.

Footwear: Walking shoes or trail sneakers with good grip. Cobblestone paths in Old Manali and uneven terrain at viewpoints will challenge sandals.

Outfit 2 — Mountain Activity (Rohtang Pass, Atal Tunnel, Light Treks)

At Rohtang Pass (3,978m), June temperatures can be near 0°C with snow on the ground. This is a completely different dressing scenario.

Warm base layer: Thermal underlayer (top and bottom) is essential. Non-negotiable.

Insulation layer: A fleece jacket or a down vest over your thermal.

Outer shell: A waterproof or windproof jacket. Snow and rain are both possible here in June.

Accessories: Gloves, a warm beanie or woollen cap, and sunglasses (UV reflection from snow is intense). Sunscreen is also essential at high altitude.

Shoes: Waterproof trail shoes or trekking boots with ankle support. Rohtang involves walking on snow and mud.

Note: You can also rent warm gear in Manali town if you don't want to pack heavy.

Outfit 3 — Evening Out (Old Manali Cafés, Restaurants, Shopping)

Evenings in Manali call for warm, comfortable but still put-together outfits. The Old Manali café scene has a relaxed, boho traveller vibe — overdressing stands out.

Top: A warm knit sweater or a cosy hoodie.

Bottom: Jeans or warm joggers.

Outer: A puffer jacket or a woollen shawl over your shoulders.

Footwear: Comfortable boots or clean trainers.

Accessories Worth Packing

  • Warm beanie or woollen cap (mandatory for higher altitudes)
  • Light gloves (not heavy ski gloves unless going very high)
  • Sunglasses with UV protection
  • Small day backpack for carrying removed layers
  • Sunscreen SPF 50+ (altitude increases UV intensity significantly)
  • A lightweight scarf that doubles as warmth

What NOT to Pack for Manali in June

  • Heavy winter coats (too much bulk for June daytime)
  • Only flip-flops or sandals (you'll be uncomfortable)
  • Only summer clothing (even if you're going in June — evenings are cold)
  • Formal shoes (impractical on uneven terrain)

Packing Summary — June Manali

The golden rule: pack for layers, not extremes. You need one outfit that works for a 25°C afternoon walk and another for a 5°C evening. The right layering system makes both possible without overpacking.
